about.title: Our story
about.intro: TailorBox is a small knit-fabric workshop in Kyiv. We cut fabric by the meter so you buy exactly as much as you need.

blocks.heading: How it started
blocks.text: We sew ourselves and know how hard it is to find good fabric in small lengths without wholesale minimums. So we built a shop where you can order from 0.5 m.

blocks.heading: What drives us
blocks.text: Honest descriptions, real photos, samples to touch and help with choosing — so fabric makes sense even to a beginner.

howWeWork.title: How we work
howWeWork.intro: From the roll to your parcel — a few simple steps.

faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.intro: The essentials if you're just starting out.

blocks.heading: How many meters for a size 86 bodysuit?
blocks.text: Roughly 0.6–0.8 m of 180 cm wide single jersey.

blocks.heading: Jersey or interlock?
blocks.text: Interlock is smooth on both sides and holds its shape. Jersey is thinner and lighter.

blocks.heading: What is weight (g/m²)?
blocks.text: The higher, the denser the fabric. Up to 180 is light, above 250 is dense.

blocks.heading: Can I order less than a meter?
blocks.text: Yes, the minimum is 0.5 m.

guide.title: How to choose fabric
guide.intro: We explain it in words a seasoned seamstress and a beginner will both understand.

blocks.heading: Knit types
blocks.text: Single jersey — light and breathable, for tees and bodysuits. Fleece — denser, brushed or not, for hoodies. Interlock — dense, holds shape. Rib — stretchy, for cuffs and necklines.

blocks.heading: Weight
blocks.text: g/m² shows density. Up to 180 is light summer, 200–250 is all-round, above 250 is warm.

blocks.heading: How much to buy
blocks.text: A size 86 bodysuit — 0.6–0.8 m, an adult tee — 1–1.5 m. Not sure — order a sample.

wholesale.intro: Sewing to sell? We work with workshops and brands.
